purpose: Field findings — the walls, measured. Empirical evidence laddering to the silence/gap thesis (principles.html). Render as a strip on the library-schema FIND-GAPS/LACUNA drawer.

insights.title: The acquisition wall, measured (Syriac)
insights.finding: Systematically probing 25 clavis-attested Syriac author-silences: 20% (5) have a public-domain, OCR-clean edition recoverable — including Jacob of Edessa and the Doctrine of Addai; 72% (18) have no digitized public-domain witness at all. The 'acknowledge' stance is not a hedge — it is the empirical majority.

detail.why: To turn NAMED silences into HELD text — test whether the LACUNA fill-loop works end-to-end on real non-Western author-gaps (LWS #1: breach the canon + Anglophone walls).
detail.expected: For obscure Syriac authors, the public-domain digitized record likely holds usable editions for only a handful (§2.8 — yield honestly modest).
detail.found: Of 25 probed — 5 fillable (PD + OCR-clean), 18 with zero Internet Archive text, 1 OCR-gibberish scan auto-rejected (the 'Swete case'), 1 rights-status-unknown flagged (not silently served).
detail.what_it_says: Most named non-Western author-silences cannot be filled from the accessible public-domain record — so NAMING the silence, with a verifiable clavis citation, is most of the value. The corpus's Western/canonical skew is partly a digitization-availability artifact, now made visible rather than masked. (Method: IA advancedsearch per clavis-author → rights-gate → OCR-gate; dry-run pilot — the 5 fillable await the v2 ingest.)

insights.title: The double silence of copyright — recovered-suppressed texts (Gospel of Mary)
insights.finding: The Gospel of Mary — suppressed and lost in antiquity, then RECOVERED only in modern critical editions — is copyright-walled, because the reconstruction and translation are post-1955. It is silenced twice: once by historical suppression (why it is non-canonical and was lost), and again now by copyright (its recovery is locked out of the public-domain corpus).

detail.why: Cataloguing the non-canonical gospels surfaced that some primaries are copyright-walled, not public domain.
detail.found: The Gospel of Mary's ANCIENT text is public domain in principle, but the only usable form — the modern critical reconstruction + translation — is post-1955 and under copyright, so it cannot be freely held or served.
detail.what_it_says: Copyright, though legitimate and important, has a regressive effect on already-silenced texts — the very act of RECOVERING a suppressed voice (a modern scholarly edition) re-locks it out of the free corpus. The double silence is structural: first the historical erasure, then the modern re-enclosure. This is NOT an argument against copyright — it makes copyright's silencing EFFECT visible (§2.8).

insights.title: The double silence of copyright — recent marginalized theologies
insights.finding: Women's, Black, Latino, and queer theologies emerged comparatively recently (in America, largely post-1960s). They are silenced twice: first by the historical and political climate that denied them a public voice; and again in the corpus, because their recent work is under copyright — not public domain — and so cannot be freely held. On the atlas-cleaned corpus (S160), the marginalized-theology copyright-walled rate is ~2.0× the Christian baseline (~11% vs ~5.5%) — directional and noise-cleaned, but bounded by an incomplete rights triage.

detail.why: Building a bottom-up cross-tradition corpus from public-domain + open-access sources — and the PI asked whether copyright's double-silence could be turned from an argument into a number.
detail.expected: A comprehensive corpus would represent liberation, feminist, Black, Latino, and queer theology alongside the canon.
detail.found: These theologies are recent, so most of their primary work falls under copyright (post-~1929) and is excluded from the public-domain corpus — the same filter that admits centuries-old canonical Western texts. Measured on the atlas-cleaned corpus (post-#2872), the marginalized-theology tags are copyright-walled at ~11% (113/1016 rights-determined) vs ~5.5% (1747/31722) for the Christian baseline — a ~2.0× gap. The noise caveat is now RESOLVED (the collision-noise was spread thin — only 111 rows in this tag — so cleanup left the ratio ~stable; my earlier ~3× prediction was disproven). The ONE remaining caveat: rights_status is 68% PENDING, so this is measured on the rights-determined minority — defensible once the rights triage advances.
detail.what_it_says: The corpus's skew is not only a digitization artifact (see the Syriac acquisition wall) — it is also a COPYRIGHT-TERM artifact. Because marginalized voices were silenced FIRST (they gained a public voice late), copyright silences them a SECOND time (their recent work is enclosed). Hold the paradox: copyright is important and legitimate AND it has this regressive, doubly-silencing effect. And the corpus cannot yet fully measure this, because two-thirds of it is un-triaged for rights — a silence about the silence.
